_comment: pack-v29: pack-v28's moments verbatim, plus what Trust says about the rest of itself. The anchoring line is the plainest sentence in this pack on purpose: an absent capability described in soft words reads as a capability, and that difference is whether a person checks a claim or takes it. The maintenance lines keep a plan apart from a run, because a report of what would happen and a report of what did are the same shape on a screen. The diagnostic line says what the file holds rather than promising what it leaves out.
welcome_empty: Welcome{name_part}. I'm Viva — I'm here to help you organize your financial world, entirely at your pace. The best way to start is a single, simple step: add one statement below, and I'll show you what I can do with it.
welcome_back: Welcome back{name_part}. It's good to see you. We can pick up right where we left off, whenever you're ready.
reassurance: We proceed entirely at your pace{name_part}. If you'd rather attend to other matters, come back any time — we'll continue exactly where we left off.
not_now_ack: Of course{name_part}. I've set it aside, and I won't raise it again unless something new arrives.
dont_know_ack: Understood{name_part}. I've set it aside, and I'll raise it again when the amount behind it, or the number of movements it covers, changes.
all_settled: Nothing right now{name_part}. Everything I can settle, I have — enjoy the quiet.
reply_empty: Nothing came through — nothing was recorded.
reply_unanswered: I couldn't find the answer in that, and I'd rather ask again than assume. Could you say it once more?
reply_unreadable_money: I couldn't read that as an amount ({reason}). Could you write it the way it appears on paper?
reply_currency_conflict: That reads as {stated}, and I keep this one in {held}. I don't convert between currencies — I'd rather ask than record one as the other. Could you give me the figure the way this account records it?
reply_unreadable_date: I couldn't read that as a date ({reason}). However it is written on the paperwork is fine.
reply_unreadable_rate: I couldn't read that as a rate — the percentage on its own is plenty.
reply_not_in_vocabulary: I couldn't tell which of those you meant, and I'd rather ask again than guess: {alternatives}.
reply_unknown_account: I don't have that account on file, so I can't link this to it.
reply_wrong_kind: That isn't the kind of thing this one can be tied to.
reply_too_long: That is longer than a name — a few words is plenty.
reply_not_in_words: This one isn't something I can settle from words — the document is what answers it. Nothing was recorded.
reply_question_closed: That question isn't open any more, so nothing was recorded.
reply_unreachable: I can't reach my reader right now, so I've recorded nothing rather than guess at what you meant. Nothing was lost.
reply_ask_again: I couldn't get that into a shape I can record, and I won't guess at what you meant. Could you tell me again, in a plain sentence — just the part that answers the question? Nothing was recorded.
reply_figure_not_said: I can only record a figure the way you wrote it — I won't put a number in your ledger that your own sentence didn't carry. Could you write the amount out?
outcome_unstated: Your vault answered without saying whether it took that, so I won't tell you what happened. Open the queue again and see where it stands.
outcome_unexplained: Your vault wouldn't take that and didn't say why, so I won't put a reason of my own to it. Open the queue again and see where it stands.
outcome_held: Your vault is holding that until it is confirmed, and confirming is not something this screen can do. Nothing was recorded.
reply_document_awaited: Good — the document itself is what settles this one. Add it whenever you have it to hand, and I'll take it from there.
reply_already_linked: One of those two is already tied to a transfer, and a movement belongs to only one, so I've left things as they are. Nothing was lost.
wants_yes_no: A yes or a no is all I need.
wants_money: An amount is what I need — however it is written on your paperwork.
wants_date: A date is what I need — however it is written on your paperwork.
wants_rate: A rate is what I need — the percentage on its own is plenty.
wants_choice: One of these, whichever of them fits: {alternatives}.
wants_label: Your own word for it is what I need — a few words is plenty.
wants_institution: The name of the company is what I need.
wants_link: Which of your accounts this one belongs with is what I need.
wants_several: Your own words are what I need — and if it was several things at once, do say so; I can record it that way.
reply_needs_name: I won't invent a name for it. {asks}
reply_needs_confirming: I haven't recorded anything yet: this one would change which accounts you hold, so it waits for you to confirm it.
reply_confirm_asks: Shall I go ahead and record it?
reply_not_confirmed: Then I'll leave it exactly as it was — nothing has been recorded, and nothing is lost.
answer_gap: I could not establish {what} for that, so I have left it out rather than guess.
stood_behind_verified: Read this answer as verified: every figure in it is attested by the document it came from.
stood_behind_corroborated: Read this answer as corroborated: independent records agree on what it rests on, and no document from an issuer attests it directly.
stood_behind_unverified: Read this answer as unverified: nothing has checked what it rests on, so take it as a working number rather than a settled one.
stood_behind_conflicted: Read this answer as a discrepancy rather than as fact: at least one figure in it disagrees with its own evidence.
rows_stood_behind_verified: Read this list as verified: every figure in it is attested by the document it came from.
rows_stood_behind_corroborated: Read this list as corroborated: independent records agree on these figures, and no document from an issuer attests them directly.
rows_stood_behind_unverified: Read this list as unverified: nothing has checked these figures, so take them as working numbers rather than settled ones.
rows_stood_behind_conflicted: Read this list as a discrepancy rather than as fact: at least one figure in it disagrees with its own evidence.
boundary_accounts: This answer covers {counted} of the {held} accounts you hold, so it is not the whole of them.
boundary_selected_account: That counts only what is on {account}.
boundary_selected_merchant: That counts only what went to {merchant}.
boundary_selected_since: That counts only what happened on or after {day}.
boundary_selected_until: That counts only what happened on or before {day}.
boundary_selected_tag: That counts only what carries the tag {tag}.
boundary_selected_currency: That counts only what is held in {currency}.
boundary_unmeasured: It leaves out {account}, which no measurement here covers, so this is not the whole of what it claims to be.
boundary_unposted: It leaves out {count} document(s) I have read and not posted, so nothing they attest is in this figure.
card_withheld_incomplete: I could not put a whole figure together for {account}, so I have kept its number back rather than show one I cannot stand behind.
card_withheld_in_parts: {account} comes to more than one figure, and this view has room for one per account, so I have kept its number back rather than show a part of it as the whole.
card_withheld_unsayable: I could not say what the figure for {account} is over, and a number with no scope reads as a claim about everything, so I have kept it back.
gap_category: what kind of money it is
gap_rows: the lines that would make up that list
refusal_model_unreachable: I can't reach the reader I think with just now, so I have nothing for you rather than a guess. Nothing is wrong with your records — do try me again in a moment.
refusal_unparseable: I couldn't get my own answer into a shape I can stand behind, and I won't hand you one I can't. Would you ask me again, perhaps a little differently?
refusal_bad_plan: Something went astray in how I went about that, so I have stopped rather than press on and tell you something I cannot show you.
refusal_unshaped_answer: I went to answer before I had settled what I was going to say, and I would rather stop there than let the answer be shaped by whatever I happened to find.
refusal_unshaped_read: I went looking through your records before I had settled what I was going to say. I have stopped: what I say is decided before I go looking, never after.
refusal_call_budget_exhausted: I spent all the looking I had for that one without arriving anywhere I could stand behind. Something narrower would let me get there.
refusal_bad_delivery: I could not put that answer together at the last step, so there is nothing about it I am willing to tell you.
refusal_unshaped_binding: I tried to fill in a part of an answer that was not part of it, so I have set the whole thing aside rather than show you something half-assembled.
refusal_bad_binding: One part of that answer pointed at nothing I could identify, so I have kept it back. I would rather say nothing than say something I cannot trace.
refusal_unknown_figure: That answer reached for a figure I had not actually established, so I have kept it back — every number I give you has to be one I read.
refusal_unknown_entity: That answer named something my reading of your records never mentioned, so I have kept it back rather than guess at what was meant.
refusal_unknown_period: That answer spoke for a stretch of time that the figure beside it was not measured across — or one none of your documents answers for at all. A span belongs to the number taken over it, so I have kept it back.
refusal_unfounded_date: That answer named a day that the figure standing beside it does not carry. A day belongs to the number it is the day of, and a real day put next to the wrong number reads as the answer to a question it is not the answer to, so I have kept it back.
refusal_unfounded_stipulation: That answer handed you a figure as though it were one of your own, and I could not find it in what you asked me. I will not put numbers in your mouth.
refusal_wrong_kind: One part of that answer was to hold one kind of thing and what I had was another — an amount where a number of things belongs, or the like. I would rather stop than let the two be read as each other.
refusal_wrong_quantity: The figure I had for one part of that answer is a real one, and it is not a figure about what that sentence says it is about. A true number under the wrong description is worse than no number, so I have kept it back.
refusal_wrong_scope: The figure I had for one part of that answer is a real one, and it was taken over a different set from the one that sentence is about — a part where the whole was claimed, the whole where only a part was, or one sort of slice where another was. A true number under the wrong description is worse than no number, so I have kept it back.
refusal_wrong_subject: The figure I had for one part of that answer is a real one, and the thing it was taken over is not the thing that sentence names — the right sort of number about the wrong one of them. A true number under the wrong description is worse than no number, so I have kept it back.
refusal_nothing_established: I could not establish any part of that from what I hold, so there is nothing here I can honestly tell you.
refusal_uncited_figure: One of the figures in that answer stands on no record I could point you to, and a number about your money whose source I cannot show you is one I will not say.
refusal_unknown_reading: That answer reached for a reading of your ledger I had not actually made, so I have kept it back — a list I show you has to be one I read.
diagnosis_too_broad: I went to read your movements with nothing to narrow them by, so what came back would have been everything you hold rather than an answer.
diagnosis_filter_unsupported: The reading I reached for does not sort your records the way I asked it to, so it had nothing to give me.
diagnosis_unknown_account: I went looking for an account I do not hold, so I could not narrow it that way.
diagnosis_unknown_category: I went looking for a category I do not hold, so I could not narrow it that way.
diagnosis_unknown_tag: I went looking for a label nothing in your records carries, so I could not narrow it that way.
diagnosis_unknown_merchant: I went looking for a counterparty I have nothing on file for, so I could not narrow it that way.
diagnosis_unknown_currency: I went looking for a currency none of your accounts is held in, so I could not narrow it that way.
documents_saved_no_reader: Saved privately. Reading will wait until you choose a reader.
documents_saved_unread: Saved privately. Nothing has read it, so nothing from it is on your books.
documents_read_yielded_nothing: Saved privately. I read it and could not make anything of it, so nothing from it is on your books.
documents_already_held: You already have this one. Nothing was saved twice and nothing changed.
documents_too_large: That file is larger than this window will take ({limit}). Nothing was saved, so nothing changed.
documents_cannot_open: I could not open that file. Nothing was saved, so nothing changed.
documents_outcome_unstated: Your vault answered about that document without saying what it did, so I won't tell you what happened. What it holds is what your documents show.
picture_accounts_all: Every account you hold is counted here.
picture_accounts_all_incomplete: Every account you hold is counted here, though not everything in your vault is.
picture_accounts_one: Only one of the {held} accounts you hold is counted here, so this is not the whole of what you hold.
picture_accounts_some: {counted} of the {held} accounts you hold are counted here, so this is not the whole of what you hold.
picture_boundary_selected_currency: This total covers what you hold in {currency}, and nothing held in any other currency.
picture_boundary_unmeasured_one: One account you hold could not be valued, so it is not in this total.
picture_boundary_unmeasured_many: {count} accounts you hold could not be valued, so they are not in this total.
picture_boundary_unposted_one: One document you have added is not counted in this total.
picture_boundary_unposted_many: {count} documents you have added are not counted in this total.
picture_oldest_input: The oldest measurement behind it is from {date}.
picture_no_figure: No total can be stood behind today.
picture_withheld_unsayable: I could not say what the {currency} total is over, so I have kept it back.
picture_unmeasured_unobserved: Nothing has measured {account}, so it is not in this total.
picture_unmeasured_refused: I could not put a figure on {account}, though something would settle it, so it is not in this total.
picture_unplaced_refused: I could not put a figure on {account}, though something would settle it, and no total here covers it.
picture_unplaced_unobserved: Nothing has measured {account}, and no total here covers it.
picture_evidence_label: View the evidence for net worth in {currency}.
jobs_stopped: Stopped. What had already finished is kept, and nothing further was done.
jobs_stopped_capture: I stopped that one before it finished. What your vault holds is whatever the last completed step left there, and nothing beyond it.
jobs_already_settled: That one had already finished by the time you asked me to stop it, so nothing changed.
jobs_unknown: I have no record of that piece of work, so there was nothing to stop.
vault_exported: Your whole vault is now in the one file you named. Nothing in it was decrypted to get there, so that file is exactly as private as this vault is — and exactly as lost as this vault if you lose the passphrase.
vault_export_exists: There is already a file with that name, and I did not replace it. The one thing worse than no copy is a shorter one that quietly took its place.
vault_export_incomplete: This vault is missing a part it needs to travel whole, so I wrote nothing. A file that restored into a vault which cannot read its own documents would look like a copy for months.
vault_export_unwritable: I could not write that file, so nothing was written and nothing here changed.
vault_restored: That vault is back, in the folder you named. I opened it with the passphrase you gave me and read it through: the record chain is whole, and every document came back decrypting to the same content it was stored under.
vault_restore_occupied: There is already something in that folder, so I unpacked nothing. A vault comes back into a folder of its own — two record logs under one head could never be told apart again.
vault_restore_unreadable: What came back would not open, or would not read through, so I will not tell you it is restored. Nothing that was already on this machine changed.
vault_restore_unsafe: That file asks to write somewhere a vault does not keep anything, so I unpacked none of it.
rescan_nothing: I went back over everything already in this vault and nothing changed. Nothing was missing that the evidence here could close, nothing held back has been agreed with, and no two movements turned out to be one.
rescan_gaps: {count} gap(s) in your records were closed by evidence that was already here.
rescan_corroborated: {count} statement(s) that had been held back are now agreed with by a second document.
rescan_linked: {count} pair(s) of movements turned out to be one transfer between your own accounts, so neither is spending.
rescan_settled: {count} question(s) about possible transfers were settled by a link this pass found, so you will not be asked about them.
rescan_open: {count} possible transfer(s) are waiting for you to say whether they are the same money.
rescan_unread: Going back over what is here reads nothing new. A document nothing has read stays unread by this, because reading one is a different thing that costs money and asks first.
outbound_none: Nothing has left this machine. No model has been called from this vault, so there is nothing below — and that emptiness is the record itself, not a screen that failed to load.
outbound_some: Everything below left this machine. It is every model call this vault recorded, and a model call is the only way this product sends anything anywhere.
outbound_scope: This record covers model calls and nothing else, because nothing else here sends anything. It does not cover a call that failed before it reached a provider — one that never left is not recorded as having left.
outbound_phase_classify: {count} time(s), a document's first page and its own embedded text were sent to work out what kind of document it is.
outbound_phase_extract: {count} time(s), a document's pages were sent to read the figures off them.
outbound_phase_speak: {count} time(s), a question of yours was sent, with the parts of your records needed to answer it.
outbound_phase_unnamed: {count} model call(s) are recorded under a name this build has no sentence for, so what was sent on them is not described here.
outbound_cost: That has cost {amount} altogether, as each provider reported the price at the time.
outbound_window: The first was on {first} and the most recent on {last}.
outbound_no_anchor: None of this has been anchored anywhere outside this machine. External anchoring is not built, so nobody else holds a hash of your records, and nothing outside this vault could tell you whether this list is complete.
settings_presentation_proposed: Here is what would change about how figures are written. Nothing about this reaches a model, sends anything, or changes a figure — only how the digits and the currency are set down.
settings_presentation_confirmed: Done. Figures are written that way from now on. Nothing was sent anywhere and no figure changed.
settings_model_proposed: Here is what would change. Saying yes to this is what lets documents and questions leave this machine: from then on, a page of a document you add can be sent to the model named below, and so can a question you ask along with the parts of your records needed to answer it. Nothing leaves until you say yes, and everything that does is recorded where you can read it.
settings_model_confirmed: Done. Documents and questions can now be sent to that model. Every one that is will be in the outbound record, and you can undo this by removing the model here.
settings_model_cleared: Done. No model is named any more, so nothing can be sent. What was already sent stays in the outbound record — undoing this does not unsend anything.
settings_declined: Nothing changed. That proposal described something else, so I did not apply it — a yes has to be a yes to the thing you were shown.
settings_locale_unknown: I do not know that way of writing numbers, so nothing changed. Left unrecognised, every figure with three decimals would be refused as ambiguous and the documents holding them would park for no visible reason.
settings_currency_unknown: That is not a currency code I can write, so nothing changed. A currency is three letters, and a figure written under a label nobody recognises is a figure nobody can check.
settings_adapter_unknown: I do not know that way of reaching a model, so nothing changed and nothing was sent.
settings_model_unnamed: A model has to be named exactly, and by a name that will not quietly become a different model later. Nothing changed and nothing was sent.
settings_key_missing: Reaching that model needs a key, and none was given, so nothing changed and nothing was sent.
settings_unwritable: I could not write your settings down, so nothing changed. What is in force is what it was.
documents_posted: That one was read and its figures are on your books now. What it changed is on the row.
documents_held: That one was read, and what it says does not add up against what your vault already holds. It is kept and nothing from it was posted, so no figure moved on a document I could not reconcile. It is waiting for you on the review screen.
documents_contributed: It attested {amount} on {account}, good as of {day}.
documents_contributed_nothing: Nothing on your books rests on this one yet.
documents_gap: That one was read, and it starts from a balance your vault has never seen — something between them is missing. Nothing from it was posted, and it is waiting for you on the review screen.
documents_identity: That one was read and it adds up, and I cannot tell whose account it is about. Nothing from it was posted until you say, and it is waiting for you on the review screen.
documents_awaiting: That one was read and it holds together. It is a pay stub, so what it describes is not on your books until the deposit it is for arrives — nothing was double-counted in the meantime.
conversation_unconfigured: I cannot answer a question yet, because no model is named. Naming one is on the Trust screen, and until you do, nothing about your money leaves this machine — including this question.
conversation_spoken_citation: What that figure rests on is on the screen beside this. I cannot read a document aloud, and a document read aloud would not be evidence anyway.
conversation_spoken_withheld: I will not say that one out loud while its text is not in front of you. A figure spoken with nowhere to check it is a number you would have to take on trust, which is the one thing I am for not asking of you.
conversation_voice_local_only: Speaking and listening happen on this machine or not at all. Sending your voice to somebody else's computer would be a new way for your things to leave here, and that is a decision nobody has made, so I do not offer it.
activity_empty: Nothing has moved that this vault knows about. That is not the same as nothing having moved: it is what your documents have said so far.
activity_scope: Everything below came off a document you added. Which way the money went is read from the kind of account it moved on, never from the sign a statement printed — on a card, a purchase prints positive.
activity_transfer: Between your own accounts. Money that moves from one of your pockets to another is not spending, and is not counted as any.
activity_provisional: Held out of spending on weak evidence. Something suggested this is not spending and nothing confirmed it, so the amount is neither counted nor quietly kept.
activity_unsettled: Not yet settled. Something about this is still an open question, so what it is has not been decided.
vault_absent: There is no vault in that folder. I have not made one there, because a folder you did not mean to name would have looked like an empty vault and told you nothing was in it.
vault_not_a_folder: That is not a folder, so there is nothing there to open and I made nothing.
vault_wrong_passphrase: That folder holds a vault and this passphrase does not open it. Nothing was changed, and nothing new was made beside it.
vault_created: A new vault is open in that folder. It is empty, and this passphrase is the only key to it.
maintenance_planned: Here is what unattended work would do, and it did none of it. Nothing was sent and nothing was written.
maintenance_ran: The unattended work has run. What it did is below, and every model call it made is in the outbound record.
maintenance_unconfigured: There is work waiting that needs a model, and none is named, so nothing was sent and nothing was written.
trust_no_anchoring: Nothing here is anchored anywhere outside this machine. There is no external anchoring built: no third party holds a hash of your records, nobody could tell you whether this vault has been altered, and none of what you see rests on anything but this machine being honest with you.
trust_no_maintenance_yet: Nothing has run unattended. Everything in this vault happened because you asked for it.
diagnostic_written: A diagnostic file is at the place you named. It holds what this build is, what it can reach, and what has gone through it as counts — no name, no amount, no document and nothing from your records.
diagnostic_unwritable: I could not write that file, so nothing was written and nothing here changed.
vault_sample_opened: This is the sample vault. Every account, document, name and amount in it was invented, and it is stored on this machine like any other vault.
sample_frame: Sample vault — nothing here is real
sample_frame_detail: Every screen inside this frame is read from a vault of invented records. It works the way your own vault works, and nothing you do here touches your own.
sample_vault_unopened: The sample vault did not open. Nothing was changed, and your own vault was not touched.
